extracted.intended_audience: Researchers applying to the DFG Emmy Noether Programme (early-career group leaders / postdocs seeking independent junior research group funding)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and eligibility rules for preparing and submitting a proposal to the DFG Emmy Noether Programme, including who may apply, required documents, timing, funding rules, and administrative/HR implications for prospective junior research group leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Where to find submission guidelines
rubrics_metrics.description: The guidelines for submitting a proposal to the Emmy Noether Programme can be found in DFG form 50.02 and the Proposal Preparation Instructions (DFG form 54.01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the specified DFG forms (links provided on the DFG site) for full instructions and required formatting/content. Use those forms as the authoritative source when preparing the proposal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals may be submitted either in German or in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Either language is acceptable; prepare the entire proposal in one of these languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date used to calculate four-year eligibility period (diploma vs oral exam)
rubrics_metrics.description: The date used to determine the four-year period is either the date on the diploma or the date of the viva voce (oral examination), depending on the individual timing of your doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no more than one year passed between presentation of the diploma and the viva voce, the date on the diploma is determining. Otherwise, the date of the oral examination is used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility period for joint doctorates
rubrics_metrics.description: For a joint doctorate (e.g. Dr. med. and PhD) the date of the first doctorate is normally used to calculate the eligibility period; a second doctorate is only taken into account if you changed subjects and your current research depends on the second doctorate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact the DFG department responsible for your subject area before submitting a proposal to determine whether the second doctorate can be used. If the second doctorate is used as the relevant date, another postdoctoral phase is required following it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Childcare periods: fixed extensions to eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Periods of childcare during a regular or previously extended proposal period give rise to a fixed 2-year extension per child for women, and a fixed 1-year extension per child for men; this applies regardless of parental leave actually taken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If evidence shows periods of childcare extending beyond one year, an extension of up to two years per child is also possible for men. The maximum extension allowed due to childcare is limited to six years for both women and men. Children under age 12 when the period begins who live permanently in the same household are included. Examples in the FAQ illustrate calculation in different birth-date scenarios. Documents accepted as evidence of periods of childcare exceeding one year include employer confirmations of parental leave or reduced hours, or official documents relating to claiming parental allowance (Elterngeld or ElterngeldPlus). Part-time employment due to childcare is taken into account proportionally; the reason for reduced hours must be clear from the document. If in doubt, contact Head Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculation examples for childcare and part-time work
rubrics_metrics.description: The FAQ provides concrete date examples showing how fixed extensions apply and how part-time work is counted proportionally (e.g., 12*50% months = 6 months added).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the examples to check how birth dates and part-time fractions change the expiry date of the eligibility period; contact DFG Head Office for ambiguous cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Location requirement for junior research groups
rubrics_metrics.description: Independent junior research groups within the Emmy Noether Programme must be based at universities or research institutions in Germany.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposals for groups based outside Germany are not eligible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial upper limits and eligible cost categories
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no financial upper limit for funding from the Emmy Noether Programme. You can apply for all the staff funding and direct project funding required to carry out your project, in addition to your own position as group leader.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Budget generously for the staff and direct project needs of the proposed research; no fixed cap will automatically exclude larger budgets, but costs should be justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to request a group leader position
rubrics_metrics.description: Normally, requests for funding from the Emmy Noether Programme must include the group leader position.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: (1) junior professors or those at a similar qualifying stage may apply to the programme as group funding without requesting a leader position for themselves; (2) researchers in clinical roles may apply for a 'rotation position' instead of a group leader position to retain clinical employment while carrying out the research (rotation position requires at least 49% of a full-time post to be retained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation position for clinicians
rubrics_metrics.description: For researchers in clinical roles it is possible to apply for a 'rotation position' (which allows you to be temporarily replaced) instead of a group leader position, so you can retain clinical employment (full-time or part-time) while conducting the funded research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rotation position requires retaining at least 49% of a full-time post. Use this option when clinical responsibilities make a full-time group leader post infeasible.

rubrics_metrics.name: No third‑party endorsements attached
rubrics_metrics.description: Please do not attach any endorsements from third parties to your proposal. Only the information provided in the proposal will be reviewed and evaluated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endorsements are not passed on to reviewers or decision-making bodies; attaching them does not benefit the applicant and is discouraged to ensure equal treatment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Average processing time
rubrics_metrics.description: The current average processing time for the Emmy Noether Programme is approximately eight months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For more details or subject-area-specific timelines, contact the DFG department responsible for your subject area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typical success rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The success rate for proposals in the Emmy Noether Programme is approximately 20% for all subject areas.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this as a planning statistic when assessing odds and considering alternative funding strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous research grant with PI position
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not possible to request a research grant with a PI position in addition to a proposal in the Emmy Noether Programme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include a separate funding request that would grant you a PI position alongside an Emmy Noether application; the two are mutually exclusive in this context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start of funding after approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of funding must be initiated within six months of the proposal being approved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan start dates and employer arrangements to comply with the six-month requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remuneration/classification: salary group 15 TV-L (DFG position)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the DFG’s view, leaders of junior research groups in the Emmy Noether Programme satisfy the prerequisites for classification within salary group 15 TV-L, but the decision on classification is a matter for the employing university or research institution in each case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification is performed on the basis of the work assigned and the TV-L work characteristics; the DFG explains legal/case-law foundations for 'high-level performance' required for group leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Points to note about TV-L salary group classification and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Assignment to salary groups and salary levels is complex: the salary group depends on the nature of the work, while salary level depends on professional experience. Higher group classification does not automatically mean higher immediate income because salary levels matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate how moving groups may lower salary if assigned to a low level. Collective bargaining law has a 'protective provision' to avoid income drops when staying with the same employer, but this generally does not apply when changing employer. Relevance of prior experience is judged by subject matter; Section 16(2)(6) TV-L (Research) allows taking into account experience not strictly 'relevant' if 'beneficial to the proposed work' in individual cases for new appointments. Performance-based allowances or bonuses are also options. Applicants are strongly urged to contact the host institution early to clarify classification and level decisions; further information is linked on the DFG site.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim report: preparation and submission deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Interim report preparation should follow the relevant guidelines (DFG form 10.22). Deadlines depend on when the proposal was submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you submitted your proposal before 31 December 2017, the interim report should be submitted no later than 6 months before the end of the second funding stage (of the fourth year) to ensure the third stage is approved in good time. If you submitted on or after 1 January 2018, submission of the interim report is essential for approval of the second stage of funding and should be submitted to the DFG 6 months before the end of the third year.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options when staff are absent due to maternal or parental leave
rubrics_metrics.description: Information on handling staff absences for maternity/parental leave is provided under Equal opportunity/Equal opportunity measures in DFG funding programmes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to the DFG Equal Opportunity page for specific measures and procedures to manage staff absences and maintain project progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of being offered a professorship during the funding period
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are offered a professorship at a German university during the funding period, project funding remains available for the remainder of the funding period; however, funds approved for your position as group leader (or rotation position) are no longer applicable and no substitute is offered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you leave the German research system, funding from the Emmy Noether Programme will end. Plan career moves and consult with DFG/host institution about implications for positions and remaining project funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal (sixth year) and family allowance for pre‑2018 submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Funding recipients who submitted proposals before the changes implemented on 1 January 2018 and who have not yet been offered a permanent professorship can submit a renewal proposal for a sixth year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The renewal proposal may be submitted earliest after the third year of funding, together with the interim report, and no later than six months before the end of the fifth year. The proposal must comply with the Proposal Preparation Instructions (DFG form 54.01) and requires an up-to-date employer’s declaration (DFG form 53.12). Applicants may also apply informally to the DFG for the family allowance for the remainder of the funding period using DFG form 41.46.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contacts for proposal and procedural questions
rubrics_metrics.description: The department responsible for the relevant specialist area at DFG Head Office will answer questions about submitting a proposal. Procedural questions can be directed to procedures-researchcareers@dfg.de.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the subject-area contacts for content/disciplinary queries and the procedures-researchcareers address for procedural/administrative questions. Further programme information and 'Funding at a Glance' links are provided on the DFG site.
